definitions.explanation: Used in formal writing to refer back to something mentioned.

examples.japanese: {同僚|どうりょう}と{昼食|ちゅうしょく}を{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I had lunch with a colleague.

examples.japanese: {同時|どうじ}に{二|ふた}つのことはできない。
examples.english: I can't do two things at the same time.

examples.japanese: {同社|どうしゃ}は{来年|らいねん}{新製品|しんせいひん}を{発売|はつばい}する。
examples.english: The said company will release a new product next year.
examples.notes: {同|どう} + {社|しゃ} = the same/said company

notes:
{同|どう}〜 is a prefix meaning 'same' or 'the said.'

COMMON COMPOUNDS (SAME):
- {同時|どうじ} (same time; simultaneous)
- {同僚|どうりょう} (colleague)
- {同級生|どうきゅうせい} (classmate)
- {同窓会|どうそうかい} (class reunion; alumni association)
- {同意|どうい} (agreement; consent)
- {同様|どうよう} (same; similar)
- {同居|どうきょ} (living together)
- {同情|どうじょう} (sympathy)

FORMAL/WRITTEN USE (THE SAID):
- {同社|どうしゃ} (the said company)
- {同氏|どうし} (the said person)
- {同日|どうじつ} (the same day; that day)

This usage appears frequently in news articles and formal writing.
